## Motivation

A generative model specifies a probability model or sampling procedure for possible data, optionally conditioned on supplied information.
A model family describes part of a system, while its architecture, loss, and [sampler]{.term key="sampler"} describe other choices.
Identifying each choice makes apparently conflicting descriptions compatible.
For robot policies, several actions can fit the same observation: a robot may reach around an obstacle from either side, while an average path passes through it.
Identify the target, model inputs, sampler, and execution procedure before comparing such policies.

## Task, architecture, loss, and generation order {#taxonomy}

Regression is the task of predicting numerical quantities.
A Transformer is an architecture, MSE is an objective component, and [autoregression]{.term key="autoregressive-model"} is a factorisation of a sequence distribution.
These describe different choices and can occur in the same system.

| Construction | What the network predicts |
|---|---|
| Direct point prediction | One action chunk from the observation. |
| Autoregressive token model | A distribution over the next token given the prefix. |
| Conditional VAE | Decoder outputs conditioned on an observation and a latent variable. |
| Noise-prediction diffusion | Noise given a noisy sample, observation, and noise level. |
| Flow matching | A velocity given a current sample, observation, and flow time. |

Autoregression is not restricted to discrete tokens; continuous autoregressive models also exist.
Likewise, a Transformer can predict an entire numerical chunk jointly.
Its architecture alone does not determine whether generation is autoregressive.

## How model families overlap {#generative-models}

A generative model defines a way to sample data, often alongside a density or a method for evaluating or estimating one.
The following descriptions overlap; they are not a partition based only on network architecture.

| Family | Mathematical construction |
|---|---|
| Autoregressive model | Factorises a joint distribution into conditional distributions. |
| Normalising flow | Transforms a base density through invertible differentiable maps. |
| VAE | Uses latent variables and a variational objective when marginalisation is difficult. |
| GAN | Trains a generator against a discriminator; a tractable generator density is not required. |
| Energy model | Specifies an unnormalised density through an energy function. |
| Diffusion or score model | Learns denoising or scores across noise levels, then uses a sampler. |
| Flow matching | Regresses a velocity field for a chosen probability path. |

An energy model explicitly specifies relative densities even when its normaliser is unknown.
Diffusion models can also have likelihood bounds or likelihood evaluation procedures; “generates samples” does not imply that density is irrelevant.
See [VAE](autoencoders.qmd#vae), [normalising flows](../../literature-review/theory/normalizing-flows.qmd), [diffusion](diffusion.qmd), and [flow matching](flow-matching.qmd).

## Factorise the sequence distribution {#factorisation}

For discrete tokens $c_1,\ldots,c_L$ and supplied context $o$, an autoregressive model represents

$$
  p_\theta(c_{1:L}\mid o)
  =\prod_{j=1}^{L}p_\theta(c_j\mid c_{<j},o).
$$

During [teacher-forced training]{.term key="teacher-forcing"}, a Transformer decoder can evaluate positions in parallel using shifted target inputs and a causal mask.
The shift aligns each prediction with the next target, and the mask restricts access to the allowed prefix.
This parallel evaluation is a property of the architecture; a recurrent autoregressive model still has sequential state dependencies.
During ordinary generation, each chosen token becomes part of the next prefix.
[Cross-entropy](../mathematics/entropy.qmd#discrete-targets) trains the categorical distributions at those positions.
A probability vector has real-valued entries even though the variable it describes takes discrete token values.

## Architecture does not determine generation order {#architecture}

Autoregression can describe continuous values as well as discrete tokens.
A Transformer can instead predict an entire numerical chunk jointly, so the presence of attention does not establish autoregressive generation.
A causal mask controls access to future positions during teacher-forced training; an ordinary autoregressive sampler still extends the prefix as it generates.
[Attention masks](attention.qmd#mask-values) define allowed reads, while [attention](attention.qmd#projections) explains the query–key–value computation.

## Tokens and robot actions {#actions}

A categorical next-token probability vector has continuous numerical entries, while the next token itself takes a discrete value.
The output variable and the numbers used to parameterise its distribution have different types.
[FAST](../../literature-review/action/fast.qmd) applies discrete tokenisation to continuous action chunks.
[Generative models](generative-models.qmd) compares autoregression with latent-variable, diffusion, and flow constructions.

## Example and boundaries

For a two-token output, the joint model is $p(c_1,c_2\mid o)=p(c_1\mid o)p(c_2\mid c_1,o)$.
Training can evaluate the second factor using the demonstrated first token; generation evaluates it using the first token actually selected by the sampler.
The two procedures use the same conditional model but can supply different prefixes.
This makes the source of each input part of the explanation, alongside the formula itself.

Each conditional distribution must be normalised on its output space, and variable-length generation also needs a stopping convention.
A sampling procedure, a tractable likelihood, and a successful fit to the data are separate properties.
Neither a generative label nor the ability to draw different outputs establishes that a model reproduces the desired distribution or respects task constraints.

## Connect a concept to a policy {#papers}

[ACT](../../literature-review/action/act.qmd) uses a [conditional VAE](autoencoders.qmd#conditioning) and temporal ensembling.
[Diffusion Policy](../../literature-review/action/diffusion-policy.qmd) learns an observation-conditioned denoising field.
[π0](../../literature-review/action/pi0.qmd) and [π0.5](../../literature-review/action/pi05.qmd) use flow-based action generation within larger vision-language systems.
[IRTC](../../literature-review/action/irtc.qmd) addresses continuity between generated chunks.

## Connections {#connections}

[Autoencoders](autoencoders.qmd) develops latent-variable models and conditional reconstruction.
[Diffusion](diffusion.qmd) learns noise predictions, while [flow matching](flow-matching.qmd) learns velocities.
[Generative sampling](../robotics/generative-sampling.qmd) explains randomness and deterministic computation.
[Energy-based models](energy-based-models.qmd) connects relative density, scores, and Langevin sampling.
[Action horizons](../robotics/action-horizons.qmd) explains when the generated commands are executed.
